transcript.text: Hi, my Bosch WAN28281GB has stopped half way through a wash and is showing E18. Water still in the drum. What does that mean?

E18 on a Bosch washing machine means 'No drainage' or 'Drain took too long'. The most common cause is a blockage in the pump filter (often caused by coins, buttons, or lint) or a kinked drain hose. A failed drain pump is less likely but possible. Please switch off and unplug the machine first. Then open the small service flap at the bottom front of the machine. Place some towels underneath as water will spill out when you open it. Slowly unscrew the filter (usually a round cap) to see if it is blocked with debris. Also, look inside the hole where the filter was and try to turn the small plastic impeller (the vanes) with your finger - does it spin freely or is it jammed?

Thanks. I've emptied the water using the little emergency hose and unscrewed the filter. It had a child's sock and a hair grip wrapped round it, plus lots of fluff. The impeller turns, slightly notchy at first and then free. Also, no burning smell, but the floor got a little wet while I drained it. What should I do next?

The 'notchy' feeling suggests an obstruction that hasn't fully cleared. Please put the filter back in securely, plug the machine back in, and run a Drain or Spin Only programme. Listen at the bottom front: does the pump hum/run? And crucially, does the water actually leave the drum? This will tell us if it's just a remaining blockage or if the pump motor has failed.
Ok, I've put the filter back and run a drain/spin programme. It drains quickly, E18 has gone and it's spinning normally now.

That’s excellent news. To help prevent this from happening again, I’d suggest checking that no small items like socks or hair grips are left in pockets or around the drum edge before washing. If you need anything else, just let me know.
